Cast.Role: Corner store owner; the neighbourhood's memory.
CARD field director. Knows more than she says.

Missions.Title: Mornings
Missions.Summary: Magnolia Street wakes up. Rosa is heading to a night shift; Pilar needs walking to school.

Objectives.Text: Talk to Mom before her shift

Missions.Title: Eastwater High
Missions.Summary: Classes, lunch-table politics, and two friends with plans.

Missions.Title: Friday Lights
Missions.Summary: The Pelicans play Channelside. The whole neighbourhood is in the stands.
OnStart: say:coach:Game's at seven. Don't make me regret putting you on the roster, Navarro.
OnComplete: history:2:Pelicans edge Channelside in a Friday night thriller

Missions.Title: First Paycheck
Missions.Summary: Lupe needs help at the store. Money is tight at home.

Objectives.Text: Work your first shift at Lupe's

Missions.Title: Rafa's Favor
Missions.Summary: Your cousin needs a small favor. Small favors are rarely small.
OnStart: say:rafa:Primo. Need a small favor. Come find me.

Objectives.Text: Drop the bag at Channelside Terminal 3
Someone is waiting at the gate

Missions.Title: The Canal Lights
Missions.Summary: A night at the ship canal with Dee and Mai. The storm out over the Gulf is doing something strange.

Objectives.Text: Meet Dee and Mai after dark

Missions.Title: Isadora
Missions.Summary: A hurricane turns toward Port Arden. Rosa is stuck at the hospital.
OnStart: say:rosa:Isadora is turning toward us and I'm stuck at the hospital. Get Pilar home and bring everything in from the yard.

Objectives.Text: In the eye of the storm — find Pilar

Missions.Title: Back on Magnolia
Missions.Summary: Eli, twenty, back from two years on offshore platforms. The street has changed.

Objectives.Text: Save $3,000 for a place of your own

Missions.Title: Static
Missions.Summary: The lights flicker when you walk into a room. It's not the wiring.
OnStart: say:pilar:Eli. The fridge light died when you slammed the door. Then it came back on. Brighter.

Missions.Title: Tests
Missions.Summary: Dee measures things nobody can explain. You might be one of them.
OnStart: say:dee:Pilar says you're 'a data set'. I'm at Steamline Coffee. Bring your weird.

Objectives.Text: Practice where no one can see (use your ability three times)
Show Dee what you can do

Missions.Title: Witness
OnStart: say:pilar:ELI. Lupe's is on fire. She's still inside.

Missions.Title: Follow the Money
Missions.Summary: Mai has a spreadsheet too. Hers has Meridian Holdings in it.
OnStart: say:mai:Heard about the shelf. We need to talk, and not on the phone.

Objectives.Text: Go to the Harbor Row Municipal Annex

Missions.Title: Shells
Missions.Summary: Money moves through Channelside at night. So does Rafa.

Missions.Title: Calloway's Canal
Missions.Summary: The canal logs are kept where the canal starts.

Objectives.Text: Wait until the Works goes quiet
Grant Calloway is waiting for you

Missions.Title: The Ordinance
Missions.Summary: After the shelf and the exposé, the council wants a list of everyone like you.
OnStart: say:hollins:I need a word, Mr. Navarro. Tonight, if you can.

Objectives.Text: Councilwoman Hollins wants to see you
The council votes at the Municipal Annex

Missions.Title: Campaign Trail
Missions.Summary: Hollins is running on Keep Arden Working. Eastwater has to show up.

Objectives.Text: Canvass Eastwater from the Community Center

Missions.Title: Abernathy
Missions.Summary: The detective has run out of patience, and out of other explanations.

Objectives.Text: Abernathy asked you to come in

Missions.Title: Landfall
Missions.Summary: A new storm, and something at Calloway Works calling to it.
OnStart: say:dee:Eli, the readings at Calloway Works are off the charts. Someone's provoking an event. With a category 4 on the way.

Objectives.Text: Something is happening at Calloway Works

Missions.Title: Who He Is
Missions.Summary: The storm is over. The city voted. Now it's your turn.

Objectives.Text: Mom is waiting on the porch

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: You're up before the alarm. Who are you and what did you do with my son?

Nodes.Speaker: player
Nodes.Text: Couldn't sleep. The Hendersons' dog was doing its opera again.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: I'm on nights all week. Pilar needs walking to school, and the light bill is on the fridge. Don't open it. Just... know it's there.

Choices.Text: I've got Pilar. And I'll look for work after school.
Mom, relax. Everything's fine.
How bad is the bill?

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Your father used to say that exact sentence in that exact voice. Go on. Lunch is in the blue bag.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Everything is always fine at sixteen. Walk your sister. Blue bag, lunch.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Bad enough that I'm glad you asked and sorry you had to. Go. Walk Pilar. We'll figure it out.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Okay, don't laugh. I rebuilt the robotics club's drive train with parts from the Delacroix scrap bin.

Nodes.Speaker: player
Nodes.Text: The same scrap bin Mr. Delacroix chased us out of with a tire iron?

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: He calls it 'inventory'. Anyway. Regional qualifier is in October. I need a driver with reflexes and no sense of self-preservation.

Choices.Text: Sign me up.
I need a job, not a hobby.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Knew it. You're the only person I know who reads a warning label as a dare.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Fair. When you're rich, you can sponsor us. Put your name on the robot. 'The Navarro'.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Navarro. You live on Magnolia, right? The canal floods your street every time it drizzles?

Nodes.Speaker: player
Nodes.Text: We have a canoe. It's a whole lifestyle.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: I'm writing about why the drainage on the east side never gets fixed but Meridian Tower got a new plaza. I need people who'll talk on the record.

Choices.Text: I'll talk. And I know half the street.
People around here don't talk to reporters.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Perfect. Bring your cynicism. It photographs well.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: They talk to someone. I'd rather it was me than a rumor.

Nodes.Speaker: coach
Nodes.Text: Navarro. Channelside's got a linebacker the size of a vending machine. You're going to run past him, not through him.

Nodes.Speaker: coach
Nodes.Text: There's a scout in the stands from Tarrow State. Doesn't mean anything. Means everything. Your call how you play it.

Choices.Text: Put me in on every down.
Just want the team to win, Coach.

Nodes.Speaker: coach
Nodes.Text: That's the spirit. Also the kind of spirit that ends up in an ice bath. Go.

Nodes.Speaker: coach
Nodes.Text: Now that's what a scout should hear. Go get 'em.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Your mother told me you're looking for work. She didn't ask me to hire you. She'd rather eat the register than ask.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Stocking, mopping, the register when I trust you. Fifteen an hour, cash in hand, and you don't touch the lottery machine.

Choices.Text: Deal. When do I start?
Fifteen? The Fuel Stop pays sixteen.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Now. Apron's on the hook. The one without the hole is mine.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: The Fuel Stop also gets robbed every other Tuesday. Fifteen and I feed you. Apron's on the hook.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Four hours, nothing broken, one customer made to smile. Here.

Nodes.Speaker: player
Nodes.Text: Sixty dollars. I'm a tycoon.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Put forty of it where your mother will find it and not ask where it came from. Keep twenty. Being broke at sixteen is a tradition, not a requirement.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: Primo! Look at you, working man. Listen, I need a favor, small thing, nothing thing.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: A bag. Terminal 3, by the canal, guy in a green cap. You drop it, you walk away, you've got two hundred bucks. That's thirteen shifts at Lupe's. I did the math.

Choices.Text: Fine. Just this once.
No. Whatever that is, no.
I'm telling Lupe you're doing this out of her parking lot.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: That's my cousin. Half now, half never, because I'm generous and you're family.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: Okay, okay. Saint Eli of Magnolia Street. Don't come crying when you're still broke at forty.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: Seriously? ...Fine. You're right. Don't tell your mom, though. She's got enough.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Evening. Detective Abernathy, PAPD. You're a long way from Magnolia Street with a bag that isn't yours.

Choices.Text: It's my cousin's. I didn't look inside. Rafa Navarro.
It's laundry. Mine.
Drop the bag and run.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: That's the first honest thing anyone has said to me this week. Go home, Eli. I'll be talking to your cousin, not you. This time.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Laundry. Sure. I'm keeping the laundry. I'm also keeping your name. Go home.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: You run. Behind you, nobody chases. You get the feeling that's worse.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Heard some things today. The street talks faster than the radio.

Choices.Text: I stayed out of it.
I told you because it was right.
I messed up, Lupe.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Good. Your cousin has a big heart and no brakes. Don't be his brakes. Be somewhere else.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: It was. It won't feel like it for a while. That's how you know.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: You did. Now you know what it costs. Most people learn that lesson later and pay more for it.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: A detective called my work. My WORK, Eli.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: I can't do this twice. I buried your father because a company decided a canal fire was an acceptable cost. I will not lose you to something even stupider.

Choices.Text: I'm sorry. It won't happen again.
I was trying to help pay the bills!

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: I know you're sorry. Sorry isn't the part I'm scared of.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: The bills are my job. You being alive at twenty is yours.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Okay, so the storm cell's eight kilometers out and the lightning's been hitting the same crane for ten minutes. Same crane. That's not how lightning works.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: I've got forty photos of the same bolt. Look. It's... it's the same shape. Every time.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: A bolt hits the crane again. For a moment the air tastes like pennies and every hair on your arms stands up. Then nothing.

Choices.Text: Let's go. Now.
Mai, send me those photos.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Agreed. Nobody tell my mother I was near a lightning rod on purpose.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Already did. Don't show anyone. Something about this feels like a story before it's a story.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: I'm not leaving my store, mijo. I've ridden out six of these.

Choices.Text: Then I'm staying to board the windows with you.
Lupe, the water was chest-high in '32 stories. Please come to our place.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Stubborn like your father. Get the plywood from the back.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: ...Your mother will make me eat. Fine. Carry the photos, not the cans.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: The wind stops. Not slows. Stops. The rain hangs in the streetlight like beads on a wire.

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: Eli. Eli, look at the trash can. It's not falling.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: A garbage can lid, a shopping cart, a stop sign bent flat — all of it is floating, motionless, in a ring around you. Only around you.
Effects: history:5:Witnesses in Eastwater describe debris frozen in the air during Isadora's eye

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: It's you. It's around you. Why is it around you?

Choices.Text: It's the pressure. The eye does weird things. Come inside.
I don't know. Don't tell anyone. Please.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: The wind comes back all at once. Everything falls. Pilar doesn't say anything else. She doesn't have to.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: She nods. The wind comes back all at once, and everything falls, and your sister holds your hand like she's the older one.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Look at those arms. The platforms fed you, at least.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Pilar made a banner. Then she decided banners were childish and made a spreadsheet of everything that changed while you were gone. It's on the fridge. Where the bills used to be.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Four years. The street's half cranes now. Meridian bought the Hendersons' place, the laundromat, the lot where you boys played.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: I still need someone on the register who doesn't steal the lottery tickets. Same fifteen. It's worth less now. Everything is.

Choices.Text: I'll take it until I find my feet.
I want more than the register this time, Lupe.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Good. Apron's on the hook. The hole is bigger.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: Good. Want it loud. This street's been too quiet about what it wants.

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: I've logged forty-one flickers since you came home. They cluster around you. Every one.

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: I was nine in the eye of that storm, Eli. I know what I saw. Don't lie to me now.

Choices.Text: You're right. Something's happening to me. I don't know what.
It's the old wiring. This house is falling apart.
You already knew. You've always known.

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: Okay. Okay. Then we do this like scientists. Dee still owes me a favor.

Nodes.Speaker: pilar
Nodes.Text: Sure. The wiring. I'll put that in the spreadsheet next to 'debris floats in hurricanes, sometimes'.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: So. Four years at Tarrow State, three at the Halvorsen Institute, and the best anomaly I've ever seen walks into my coffee shop.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Here's the deal: I can measure it. Field strength, range, what it costs you. But measurements go in a log, and logs get subpoenaed.

Choices.Text: Measure everything. I need to know what I am.
No logs. You watch, you tell me, you forget.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Science. Beautiful. Find somewhere empty after dark — Cypress Bend Park at two a.m. is basically a vacuum — and push it. Three times.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Off the books. My advisor would kill me. Go practice somewhere empty. Three times. Then we talk.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Your peaks line up with the canal-strike frequency from the night we were at Terminal 3. Same shape. Mai's photos, remember?

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: That's not a coincidence, man. Something at that canal did this to you, and it's been doing it on a schedule.

Choices.Text: Then we find out who owns the schedule.
I don't want to be a pattern. I want to be left alone.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Mai's been circling Calloway for a year. You should talk to her. Carefully.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Nobody gets left alone in this town, Eli. The canal made sure of that.

Nodes.Speaker: narrator
Nodes.Text: The shelving has come down across the back door. Lupe is on the floor behind it, coughing. Six neighbours are filming from the sidewalk.

Choices.Text: Lift it. All of it. Right now, in front of everyone.
Effects: history:4:Witnesses say a man lifted a burning wall of shelves off Lupe Salazar with his bare hands

Choices.Text: Go in through the storeroom window and drag her out the hard way.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: I saw it, mijo. I saw what you did. ...Everybody saw what you did.

Nodes.Speaker: lupe
Nodes.Text: You came through the window. Of course you did. Tomás used to come through that window when the door stuck.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Detective Abernathy. We met once, years ago. You were a kid with a bag that wasn't yours.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Neighbours are telling me a story about a shelf. I'm the kind of person who likes to hear stories more than once.

Choices.Text: People see what they want to see in a fire.
I went through the window. Ask Lupe.
Then you should hear it from me. Not here.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: They do. They also film it. Stay in town, Mr. Navarro.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: I will. And she'll tell me you're a good boy, and I'll believe her. Mostly.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: That's the first interesting thing anyone's said to me this year. My card.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Sixty-one lots on Magnolia, Pecan and Lafitte. Bought within ninety days of Isadora by three companies that didn't exist before the storm.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: All three have the same registered agent: a law office that does all of Meridian Holdings' paperwork. I need the deed transfers. The annex won't give them to a reporter.

Choices.Text: They'll give them to a resident asking about his own street.
Why do you need me? Because of the shelf?

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: That's exactly what I was hoping you'd say. The records room is on the second floor.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Because you're from Magnolia Street, and because I trust you. The shelf is a separate conversation. A long one.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Look at the dates. Every one of these lots flooded because the canal gates on Calloway's side were opened during the storm. Opened. Not failed.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Somebody flooded Eastwater on purpose and then bought it cheap. I can print that. Or I can wait until I can prove who.

Choices.Text: Print what you can prove. People deserve to know now.
Effects: history:4:The Arden Ledger: Meridian bought 61 flooded Eastwater lots through three shell companies

Choices.Text: Wait. If you go early, they bury it.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Tomorrow's front page. They'll come after me for it. They'll come after you too, if they know you helped.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Then we get the rest. The money has to move somehow, and money in this city moves through Channelside.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: Primo. Of all the docks. ...You're not here for the view.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: It's cash from Meridian contractors to a Tidewater guy, then to a church that doesn't have a building. I just carry it. I don't count it.

Choices.Text: Then help me count it. Talk to Mai. On the record.
I didn't see you. Give me a cut and I never will.
I'm calling Abernathy. I'm sorry, Rafa.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: You know what they do to people who talk? ...Yeah. Okay. For Tomás. Not for you. For Tomás.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: That's my cousin. Thought the platforms made you boring.

Nodes.Speaker: rafa
Nodes.Text: You did this to me once already, you know that? Go on. Call her.

Nodes.Speaker: calloway
Nodes.Text: The canal logs. Of course. You know what they don't show? The ten thousand jobs this city loses if the port stays a swamp.

Nodes.Speaker: calloway
Nodes.Text: Your father's settlement was never going to be paid. I can fix that tonight. The Navarros get what they were owed, with interest, and those logs go back in the drawer.

Choices.Text: Pay my family. Keep your drawer.
You flooded my street. The logs are leaving with me.
Let me show you what your canal did to me.

Nodes.Speaker: calloway
Nodes.Text: A practical man. Your father would have made the same choice. Most people do.

Nodes.Speaker: calloway
Nodes.Text: Then we'll do this the expensive way. For both of us.

Nodes.Speaker: calloway
Nodes.Text: ...So it worked. Rao said it might. Get out of my building before I decide what you're worth.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Did you get them?

Choices.Text: Here. Every gate opening, signed.
Effects: history:5:Ledger exposé: Calloway Chemical opened the canal gates during Isadora; CARD tests preceded the storm's anomaly

Choices.Text: I... couldn't. It's complicated.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: This is it. This is the whole thing. Eli — thank you. Get somewhere safe tonight.

Nodes.Speaker: mai
Nodes.Text: Complicated. Okay. I'll find another way. I always do.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: The Arden Renewal people want a registry. Name, address, ability. They say it's safety. I say it's a list, and lists end up in the wrong hands.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: I don't know what you are and I'm not asking. I'm asking what you'll do when it passes.

Choices.Text: I'll register. Publicly. Let them see a face that isn't a monster.
I'll speak against it at council. On the record.
I'll stay out of sight and out of the registry.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: Brave. Maybe foolish. Probably both. Come to the vote anyway.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: Then come to the Annex. Sit in the front row. Let them look at you.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: I understand. I also understand what happens to people the list doesn't find.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: They voted.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: She lets the silence sit for a moment.

Choices.Text: And?
And?

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: It passed. Unregistered use in public is a crime starting tonight. I'm running for mayor, Eli. I'd like to repeal it.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: It failed. Narrowly. They'll try again after the election, which is why I'm running for mayor.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: Doors knocked, people registered, and a story about a shelf that won't die. How do you want to help from here?

Choices.Text: Put me on a stage. The shelf guy, for Hollins.
I'll organise Magnolia Street. Quietly. Door by door.
I'll give what I can.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: Then we lean into it. Visibility has a price. So does silence.

Nodes.Speaker: hollins
Nodes.Text: That's how this city actually gets won. Thank you.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: I've got a shelf, a canal log that walked out of Calloway Works, and a cousin who knows more than he says. All of it has your shape.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: I'm about to be put in charge of a special unit for people like you. I'd rather have you on the right side of my desk.

Choices.Text: Here's the truth: Calloway caused Isadora's event. I can prove it. I'll help you, not him.
I don't know what you're talking about, Detective.
Arrest me or let me go.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Then when it comes — and it's coming, the storm models look bad — you call me before you do anything spectacular.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Nobody ever does. Go home, Mr. Navarro. Watch the weather.

Nodes.Speaker: abernathy
Nodes.Text: Not today. But I keep very good notes.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: You shut it down. The rig's slag, the gates held, and Calloway's people scattered when the tanks started venting.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: There's news helicopters, man. And twenty phones on the levee. What happened in there?

Choices.Text: Let them see. I'm done hiding what I am.
Effects: history:5:Across Port Arden, video shows a man holding back the Calloway canal gates as Hurricane Nadia made landfall

Choices.Text: It was dark. Nobody saw anything. Let's keep it that way.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: Then we'd better go home before they find out which home.

Nodes.Speaker: dee
Nodes.Text: It was dark. Sure. I'll back that up in any report you want.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: The polls closed while you were out there. I watched the returns in the break room with a patient who kept saying he knew you.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: So. Tell me what we won.

Choices.Text: Hollins won. The exposé stuck. Eastwater gets its lots back.
Effects: ending:saved:Eastwater Community Land Trust buys back the Meridian lots after Mayor Hollins' first vote

Choices.Text: Calloway's money is in our account. Meridian keeps building.
Effects: ending:sold:Meridian breaks ground on the Eastwater waterfront towers

Choices.Text: Some of it we saved. Some of it we didn't.
Effects: ending:split:Eastwater, divided: the land trust keeps Magnolia Street while Meridian keeps building south of Pecan

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: Your father would have loved this porch tonight. Eat something. Then go be whoever you're going to be.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: The bills are paid, mijo. I just don't know what it cost. I don't think you do either.

Nodes.Speaker: rosa
Nodes.Text: That's most victories, Eli. Half a street. Come inside, it's going to rain again.

Shots.Speaker: narrator
Shots.Text: Eastwater wakes up the way it always has: early, loud, and a little behind on everything.

Shots.Speaker: player
Shots.Text: Sixteen years on Magnolia Street. Nothing ever happens here.

Shots.Speaker: narrator
Shots.Text: Cranes over Eastwater. New buildings with old names. Some doors closed for good.

Shots.Speaker: narrator
Shots.Text: Mai writes for the Ledger now. Dee measures things at Tarrow State that nobody can explain.

Shots.Speaker: narrator
Shots.Text: The storms will come back. So will the elections, the cranes and the canal lights. Port Arden keeps going.

CastChanges.Note: Graduate student at the Halvorsen Institute, Tarrow State.
Served time; out on parole and trying to stay out.
Runs a stall at the Night Market. Nobody asks what's under the counter.

Headlines: Meridian Holdings completes purchase of flood-damaged Eastwater lots
Federal anomaly directorate opens a field office at the Port of Arden
Four years after Isadora, Eastwater rebuilds — on whose terms?
Effects: say:pilar:Welcome home. I made a spreadsheet.
